description:
Improper input validation in non-secure-callable (NSC)
veneer functions of the NXP MCUXpresso SDK rpmsg-lite multicore example
(multicore_examples/rpmsg_lite_pingpong_tzm) up to releases 26.06.00-lts and
26.09.00 may allow a non-secure caller to supply unvalidated pointers and size
values, potentially resulting in disclosure of secure-world memory to the
non-secure domain, or denial of service. All software versions starting from
26.06.01-lts and 26.12.00-pvw1 have fixed this issue.

Improper handling of non-secure-world input in NSC veneer
functions of NXP MCUXpresso SDK TrustZone-M examples (trustzone_examples),
affecting versions through 26.06.00-lts and 26.09.00-pvw2, may allow a
non-secure caller to supply unvalidated pointers or untrusted data, causing a
timing side-channel, TOCTOU condition, or format-string misuse, potentially
resulting in secure-world memory disclosure or denial of service. All software
versions starting from 26.06.01-lts and 26.09.00 have fixed this issue.

UgCS server before 6.2 contains an authentication bypass in the HCI protocol login handler (LoginHandler) exposed on TCP port 3334. When the user database contains exactly one user (the default single-operator installation), a LoginRequest with empty userLogin and userPassword fields is interpreted as \"use the only user\" rather than as invalid credentials, and the server returns a fully authenticated session. Because the service listens on all interfaces (0.0.0.0) without TLS by default, an unauthenticated remote attacker with network access to port 3334 can obtain an authenticated session without knowing any credential and then issue privileged commands, including commanding connected drones and uploading flight routes.

The ZSIRep client library (ZSIREP.CLIENT.DLL) is vulnerable to improper server certificate validation. It registers a process-wide .NET callback that accepts any certificate for HTTPS connections without verification. This allows a man-in-the-middle attacker to impersonate the ZSIRep server and intercept or modify authentication data and documents. The callback persists after the client is closed, weakening other HTTPS connections in the same application.


The issue was fixed in version 2.12.3.1. The library is used in KS-SOMED (fixed in 2026.03.0.01), KS-PPS (fixed in 2026.03.1.0), KS-MEDIS (fixed in 2026.03.0.0), KS-SOLAB (fixed in 2026.3.1.0), and KS-ASW (fixed in 2026.3.0.1).
